task.description:
WF-03 Step 03b for ISS-0201: closing gate on DOC-UPDATER's Step 03. Hard gate -- PASS or FAIL, and a FAIL routes back to DOC-UPDATER as rework (rework_count is 0 of 3).

WHAT TO GATE: commits 2c5ce05 (content) and af5ad67 (git_evidence backfill) on main, against handoffs/WF03-ISS0201-20260821/step-03-riders.json's task.acceptance_criteria and its result.summary. Review `git show 2c5ce05` as the diff of record. The three riders as originally stated are in handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json result.issues -- your own findings from the ISS-0198 run. They are not restated here.

DO NOT take result.summary's verifications on trust. Re-run them first-hand and quote yours, not the producer's: extract the section 2 JSON fence and json.loads it; confirm docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md are untouched by 2c5ce05 and still carry pointer-only wording; confirm the edits are additive against the pre-edit section 2 (nothing deleted but the one bullet line rider 2 extends).

THE TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS DOC-UPDATER FLAGGED FOR THIS GATE -- rule on both explicitly, do not defer them:
(a) Rider 1 was resolved in prose with the fence left byte-identical, on the reasoning that section 4.1(b)'s backfill_note exception is SPENT and file-scoped, so adding the member to the general schema block would trade a mis-read for a real widening. Decide whether that reasoning holds, and specifically whether ISS-0191's linter can implement the not_agent_attested member check from what section 2 plus section 4.1(b) now say -- a linter author is the reader this rider exists to protect.
(b) Rider 3's resolution is a per-SOURCE check, and DOC-UPDATER's own recommendation is that it be gated by APPLYING it rather than by reading it. Apply it: take the ISS-0198 run's AC5 re-draft (handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/redraft-ISS0109-step-02-code-designer.md, the artefact whose omission is rider 3's evidence) and run the new check against it. Report whether the check, followed literally by a weak model, catches the four-dropped-restatements/one-added-path miss. If it does not catch it, that is a FAIL of ISS-0201's rider-3 acceptance criterion.

Also confirm ISS-0201's own bookkeeping is honest: docs/issues/ISS-0201.yaml status and resolution block, and the single appended docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml entry (append-only -- zero deletions).

SCOPE LIMIT: gate what this run changed. Section 2's pre-existing structure, its redundancy-not-brevity rationale, and the H-SIZE thresholds are ISS-0198's settled output and are not reopened here. Anything you find outside this run's diff is a NEW issue in result.issues at its own severity, not a FAIL of this step -- ORCH files it.

Write your verdict into this handoff and commit it. Modify no file outside handoffs/. Do NOT write handoffs/registry.json.
acceptance_criteria: A PASS or FAIL verdict is stated, with each of Step 03's eight acceptance criteria addressed individually
Rider 1's prose-not-fence resolution is ruled on explicitly, including whether ISS-0191's linter can implement the not_agent_attested member check from section 2 plus section 4.1(b) as they now read
Rider 3's check is APPLIED to handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/redraft-ISS0109-step-02-code-designer.md, and the result of applying it is reported -- not merely an opinion on its wording
The section 2 JSON fence is parsed first-hand under json.loads and the reviewer's own result is quoted verbatim
core-directives.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md are confirmed untouched by 2c5ce05 and still pointer-only, verified first-hand
The diff is confirmed additive and scoped to the three seams, with any deletion named and justified
Any finding outside this run's diff is reported in result.issues at its own severity rather than gating this step

result.summary:
PASS. Gated commits 2c5ce05 (content) and af5ad67 (git_evidence backfill) on main against step-03-riders.json's eight acceptance criteria. Every verification below was re-run first-hand; DOC-UPDATER's result.summary was read for its claims and then set aside as evidence.

VERDICT PER STEP-03 ACCEPTANCE CRITERION.
AC1 (each rider applied or declined with reason) -- MET. All three APPLIED, none declined, and 'git show 2c5ce05 -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md' shows exactly three hunks, one per rider: rider 1 a new paragraph after the 'Exactly two fields ... are OPTIONAL' sentence (+11 lines); rider 3 a check-shaped clause after the 'the reproduction is the defect' paragraph (+18 lines); rider 2 an extension of the context.requirement_text bullet (+8/-1). No fourth hunk.
AC2 (fence stays linter-loadable without rejecting the one 4.1(b)-authorised file) -- MET; ruled on in full under JUDGEMENT (a) below.
AC3 (rider 2's seam settled) -- MET. The bullet now reads 'A value under a REQ-ID key is that requirement's description and nothing else', names the split as by FIELD not by file, and enumerates the four cases that go to source_text keyed "docs/requirements.yaml" (acceptance_criteria, depends_on, owner, raw entry YAML). The seam ISS-0198's rider 2 named is closed in both directions.
AC4 (rider 3 checkable by a weak model) -- MET; ruled on by APPLICATION under JUDGEMENT (b) below.
AC5 (nothing duplicated into core-directives.md / ORCHESTRATOR.md; both untouched) -- MET, verified first-hand two ways. (i) 'git show --name-only --format= 2c5ce05' lists exactly four paths -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, docs/issues/ISS-0201.yaml, docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0201-20260821/step-03-riders.json -- and grepping that list for 'core-directives|ORCHESTRATOR' returns nothing (exit 1). (ii) Grepping both files for 'artifacts_in|task.description|H-SIZE|6,000|6000' returns only pointer lines, no rule and no threshold: core-directives.md:206-208 ('That rule is stated once, in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md S2 ("What goes in task.description, and what goes in artifacts_in"), and deliberately not restated here.') and ORCHESTRATOR.md:159-160 ('That section is canonical and this line does not restate it.'). Both still pointer-only.
AC6 (fence parses under json.loads, result quoted verbatim) -- MET. Extracted the section 2 json fence from the post-commit working tree and ran json.loads. My own output, verbatim:
    json.loads OK; top-level keys: 18
    top-level: ['handoff_id', 'run_id', 'workflow_id', 'step', 'from_agent', 'to_agent', 'file', 'created_at', 'started_at', 'completed_at', 'status', 'priority', 'context', 'task', 'result', 'rework_count', 'max_rework', 'not_agent_attested']
    context keys: ['stage', 'requirement_ids', 'requirement_text', 'source_text', 'related_handoff_ids', 'artifacts_in', 'owned_modules']
    not_agent_attested members: ['reconstructed_by', 'reconstructed_at', 'reason', 'fields_written', 'evidence', 'not_verifiable_after_the_fact']
I additionally re-extracted the fence from 2c5ce05~1 and compared bytes: 'fence byte-identical pre/post: True 2279 2279'. So the fence is not merely still parseable, it is unchanged, and the six-member reading the new paragraph asserts about it is true of the actual object.
AC7 (existing handoff files stay valid; verified over handoffs/, not asserted) -- MET. json.load over every *.json under handoffs/ except registry.json: 'parseable: 605 unparseable: 0'. DOC-UPDATER reported 604; that is not a discrepancy -- this very handoff file was created at 09:56:06Z, after its 09:54:00Z completion. Schema-affecting change this run: none, which is the strongest form of OPTIONAL-BY-ABSENCE (no new field exists to be absent from anything).
AC8 (additive, scoped, otherwise unchanged) -- MET. 'git show --numstat' gives 37/1 on HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, and filtering the diff for deleted lines ('^-[^-]') returns exactly ONE: '  changes that.' That is the last line of the context.requirement_text bullet, re-emitted as the head of the extended bullet inside the same hunk -- a continuation, not a removal, and it is the single deletion DOC-UPDATER named. No table row, no rationale paragraph, no H-SIZE spec and no fence byte was touched.

JUDGEMENT (a) -- RIDER 1 RESOLVED IN PROSE WITH THE FENCE UNCHANGED: the reasoning HOLDS, and I endorse it as the better of the two options rather than merely tolerable. The fence is the machine-loadable schema; a linter deriving not_agent_attested's member set from it gets the SIX REQUIRED members and nothing else. Had backfill_note been added to the fence, a fence-derived validator would admit that member on ALL 605 handoff files -- converting a SPENT exception that named exactly one file into a general permission, which is precisely what S4.1(b)'s no-backfill rule exists to prevent. The cost avoided (one linter author's mis-read of one file) is strictly smaller than the cost that would have been incurred (a real schema widening no later reader could undo). The prose resolution is the right trade.
CAN ISS-0191's LINTER IMPLEMENT THE not_agent_attested MEMBER CHECK FROM SECTION 2 PLUS S4.1(b) AS THEY NOW READ? YES -- I checked by deriving the rule myself, as a linter author would, from those two passages only:
  - REQUIRED set = the six members of the fence's not_agent_attested object, machine-loadable via json.loads (quoted verbatim above). Section 2's new paragraph states in terms that the fence 'shows that object's six REQUIRED members only, deliberately', so a reader knows the fence is this object's floor and not its whole set.
  - OPTIONAL set = {backfill_note}, named in section 2's new paragraph and again in S4.1(b)'s member table, whose row is marked '(OPTIONAL -- the only one)'.
  - The set is CLOSED at seven: S4.1(b) says so explicitly -- 'The member set is CLOSED at those seven, and backfill_note is the only optional one. A member that is neither required nor backfill_note is a defect, not an extension -- that is the point of enumerating them, and it is what lets ISS-0191's linter reject a misspelled or junk key.' So the reject-unknown-key rule the rider worried about is available.
  - The allowlist is a single named path: S4.1(b) names handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json as the one authorised carrier, and it is the repository's only holder of the member.
That is a complete, judgement-free specification: required = 6 (loaded), optional = 1 (transcribed), set closed, allowlist = 1 path (transcribed). Nothing is left to be inferred. Section 2's new paragraph also pre-empts the exact failure the rider named, saying a linter that 'derives the set from this fence alone and rejects the one authorised file carrying backfill_note has mis-read this paragraph, not found a defect.' AC2 is met.

JUDGEMENT (b) -- RIDER 3'S CHECK APPLIED, NOT READ. I ran the new clause literally against handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/redraft-ISS0109-step-02-code-designer.md, the artefact whose omission is rider 3's own evidence. Method, exactly as a weak model would execute it: (1) enumerate the sources whose text the re-draft removed -- its own 'What was removed, and where it already lived' table lists five rows, naming step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json (two rows), step-02b-code-design-validator.json (two rows), and docs/issues/ISS-01{07,10,11,13}.yaml; (2) build the re-draft's effective artifacts_in -- the source handoff's nine paths, read first-hand out of handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json, plus the one path the re-draft states it added; (3) ask the clause's yes/no question per SOURCE. My result, verbatim:
    handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json       YES
    handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02b-code-design-validator.json     YES
    docs/issues/ISS-0107.yaml                                              NO
    docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml                                              NO
    docs/issues/ISS-0111.yaml                                              NO
    docs/issues/ISS-0113.yaml                                              NO
    failures: 4
THE CHECK CATCHES THE MISS, and catches it at the exact shape rider 3 described: four dropped restatements, one added path. Three properties made it catch rather than pass. It is per-SOURCE, so the four issue records cannot hide behind the two sources that were satisfied. It names the ID case explicitly -- 'including one now named only by an ID (ISS-0113, REQ-042, "the design doc")' -- and ISS-0113 is literally one of the four sources missed here, so a reader matching the exemplar against their own case cannot miss it. And it closes the arithmetic escape by name: 'So does dropping four restatements and adding one path -- count the sources, not the edits.' A weak model following it literally reaches 'failures: 4' by string search alone, with no judgement exercised. The prior wording ('belongs as a PATH in context.artifacts_in', a cell in a two-column table) is what the re-draft's own author read and still shipped the miss; the new clause is answerable where the old one was only describable. AC4 is met.

ISS-0201's OWN BOOKKEEPING -- HONEST. docs/issues/ISS-0201.yaml: 35 insertions, 1 deletion, the deletion being 'status: open' replaced by 'status: resolved', plus resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0201-20260821, resolved_at: 2026-08-21T09:52:36Z, and a resolution block describing all three riders as applied and stating the fence was deliberately not changed -- which matches the diff I measured, including its claim that no file outside that one and this record was touched. docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml: numstat '36 0' -- zero deletions, re-verified independently by counting removed lines in the diff (0) -- one event appended at the tail (req: SCOPE-CHANGE, event: done, agent: DOC-UPDATER, at 2026-08-21T09:52:36Z), and SCOPE-CHANGE has two prior uses in the file, so it is not a value invented here. I re-ran the invariant suite myself rather than taking the quoted figure: 'mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs' -> 'Result: 13 passed'. af5ad67 touches only step-03-riders.json's result.git_evidence.commit_sha_list, adding 2c5ce05 -- a commit cannot cite itself, so the two-commit split is correct and not a post-hoc edit of a gated artefact.

RIDERS: three MINOR, none gating -- one seam inside this run's diff, two outside it. See result.issues.

issues.description: IN THIS RUN'S DIFF, non-gating. Rider 3's check closes with 'If any answer is no: add the path, or put the text back. There is no third option.' The second branch is stated without a destination, and section 2's own table classifies a restatement sitting in task.description prose as the defect -- so a weak model taking 'put the text back' literally reverts to the very fault the surrounding subsection forbids. The clause's preceding sentence already says both states are defects ('it is the same defect as the restatement, pointing the other way'), so this is an internal wording seam rather than a rule conflict, and the paragraph four lines below ('it travels in a structured field keyed by its source -- never in task.description prose') supplies the missing destination by adjacency. It does not gate: the branch a reader will actually take is 'add the path', which is the compliant one, and the failure mode errs toward keeping context rather than losing it. Fix if the file is amended again: '...or put the text back -- into context.source_text, never into task.description prose.'

OUTSIDE THIS RUN'S DIFF (pre-dates it; arrived with S4.1(b)). The backfill_note allowlist that section 2's new paragraph now delegates to is a single filename stated in S4.1(b)'s prose, not in any machine-loadable structure, and the optional member's name is likewise prose-only. ISS-0191's linter can implement the member check regardless -- established under JUDGEMENT (a): the required set loads from the fence, and the optional member name plus the one authorised path are one hand-transcribed constant each -- so this is an ergonomic cost, not a blocker. Worth ISS-0191's implementer knowing that two of the four inputs to this check come from prose and will not track a later edit to S4.1(b) automatically. Raised for ORCH to append to ISS-0191, not a fault of Step 03.

OUTSIDE THIS RUN'S DIFF, and about this handoff rather than the work gated. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md S1 step 3 says the receiving agent must NOT write started_at ('ORCH stamps it immediately before dispatching you'), while this step's dispatch instructed me to set it from a clock reading. Per S1.1 I am reporting the conflict rather than silently resolving it either way: I complied with the dispatch and stamped started_at 2026-08-21T09:57:14Z from 'date -u', which is after created_at 09:56:06Z and before completed_at, so timestamp monotonicity holds and no false ordering entered the record. ORCH should decide whether S1's rule or the dispatch pattern changes, since a dispatch that routinely delegates this field makes S1's stated rule dead text.

result.next_action: PASS -- Step 03 stands as committed; no rework, rework_count stays 0 of 3. ORCH: update registry.json for steps 03 and 03b, push main, then release queue task 201 / close GH#392. Three MINOR riders in result.issues -- the first is a one-clause wording fix in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 that can ride the next amendment to that file rather than reopening this run; the second belongs appended to ISS-0191's scope; the third is a protocol-versus-dispatch conflict on started_at for ORCH to settle at the source.
